The first layer filters by spatial locality—only pages 1–2 contain meaningful content. This aligns with a signal-to-noise ratio optimization principle where information density varies across document space. The second layer applies temporal coherence, assuming recent updates correlate with relevance. This is modeled as an exponential decay function of time since last update. The third layer enforces methodological rigor through completeness checks, rejecting entries lacking sufficient documentation. These primitives form a hierarchical Bayesian network within GSI, where each filter reduces posterior uncertainty. Failure modes include overfitting to outdated signals, misclassifying legitimate but sparse documents, and ignoring domain-specific naming conventions like 'NFL' in AI contexts. Dualities emerge between temporal freshness and documentation depth, both contributing to signal strength. The system must also account for adversarial noise such as spam mirrors, which can be detected via entropy thresholds.
